builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
summary: DREAM replaces external memory-isolation or continuous online-auditing modules for defending LLM agents against memory poisoning with an agent-intrinsic, training-free three-stage pipeline (perturbation-induced reactivation, anomaly diagnosis, selective memory suppression and reinforcement). It requires no model training and fits a single-GPU or API-based stack, but adds per-step inference overhead for reactivation and diagnosis, and its cost depends on how often repair passes must run. It can fail through false positives that suppress benign memories, degraded robustness against adaptive attackers not covered in the evaluation, and the need to revalidate detection thresholds for each memory backend and task distribution.
rationale: The defense is training-free and infrastructure-light, making it feasible on constrained setups, but its detection thresholds and suppression behavior must be validated against the reader's own memory store, attackers, and utility metrics before production adoption.
technique: Training-free memory repair for poisoned LLM agents

claims.statement: DREAM replaces external memory-isolation or continuous online-auditing modules for defending LLM agents against memory poisoning with an agent-intrinsic, training-free three-stage pipeline (perturbation-induced reactivation, anomaly diagnosis, selective memory suppression and reinforcement). It requires no model training and fits a single-GPU or API-based stack, but adds per-step inference overhead for reactivation and diagnosis, and its cost depends on how often repair passes must run. It can fail through false positives that suppress benign memories, degraded robustness against adaptive attackers not covered in the evaluation, and the need to revalidate detection thresholds for each memory backend and task distribution.
Up to 2.13x speedup and 37.7% reduction in token consumption versus A-MemGuard, with over 95% reduction in attack success rate against backdoor poisoning.
